document.title: The taxpayer's own record of the other itemized deductions on the Schedule A line 16 closed list

boxes.label: Gambling losses (gambling losses include, but aren't limited to, the cost of nonwinning bingo, lottery, and raffle tickets) but only to the extent of gambling winnings reported on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8b
Casualty and theft losses of income-producing property (including losses from financial scams) from Form 4684, lines 32 and 38b, or Form 4797, line 18a
Federal estate tax on income in respect of a decedent
A deduction for amortizable bond premium (for example, a deduction allowed for a bond premium carryforward or a deduction for amortizable bond premium on bonds acquired before October 23, 1986)
An ordinary loss attributable to a contingent payment debt instrument or an inflation-indexed debt instrument (for example, a Treasury Inflation-Protected Security)
Deduction for repayment of amounts under a claim of right if over $3,000
Certain unrecovered investment in a pension
Impairment-related work expenses of a disabled person
Net Qualified Disaster Loss
boxes.notes: Figured on Form 4684 line 15, never by the client; listed on the dotted line next to Schedule A line 16 (i1040sca Line 16).

document.notes: THIS IS A CLOSED LIST, and that is the point of declaring it. The 2025 Instructions for Schedule A introduce it with 'Only the expenses listed next can be deducted on line 16.' The old miscellaneous itemized deductions subject to the 2% floor - unreimbursed employee expenses, tax preparation fees, investment advisory fees - are NOT on it and have not been deductible since 2018. Gambling losses are capped at gambling winnings; a net gambling loss is never deductible. A net qualified disaster loss also reaches line 16 rather than line 15, by the route the line 16 instructions set out.

extraction.note: A taxpayer's own record. No prescribed layout, so no structured model and no boxes to read: it prints ITEMS in the client's own words, and which declared box each belongs in is a JUDGEMENT a person confirms (spec 075 group D, clarification Q1). Read by the declared custom model in TRANSCRIBE mode - the same reader, a second template - which copies every line verbatim and names no destination. A separate, cheap proposal call then suggests a box per item; **only a box a person confirms places anything**, so an engagement with nineteen rental sheets shows an empty Schedule E until somebody has looked. That is the decision, not a defect.
